units.t: Addition and Subtraction of Whole Numbers

unit.title: Addition and Subtraction of Whole Numbers
unit.blurb: Using a symbol for a missing number or operation, adding and subtracting numbers with up to 3 digits, and rules about odd and even numbers.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use a symbol to represent a missing number or operation in a number sentence.

O2.t: Estimate, add and subtract whole numbers with up to three digits.

O3.t: Use the properties of odd and even numbers to generalise about sums and differences.

sections.title: Using a symbol to represent a missing number or operation

p: A shape can stand for a missing number: in **▲ + 25 = 60**, ▲ = 35.
A missing **operation** can be +, −, × or ÷: 12 ○ 4 = 3 means 12 **÷** 4 = 3.

sections.title: Addition and subtraction of whole numbers

p: Line up hundreds, tens and ones. **Exchange** when a column makes 10 or more (adding) or is too small (subtracting).
Estimate first by rounding: 487 + 236 ≈ 490 + 240 = 730. Check by using the inverse.
In 402 − 167, exchange from the hundreds through the tens.

sections.title: Generalising with odd and even numbers

p: **even + even = even**, **odd + odd = even**, **odd + even = odd**. The same rules work for subtraction.
Test a rule with examples, and look for a counter-example that breaks it.
Only the ones digit tells you if a number is odd or even.

rubric.pt: each odd number has one left over when paired
the two left-overs make a pair

req.model: When you make pairs, each odd number has one left over. The two left-overs make one more pair, so the total has no left-over: it is even.
